blocks.content: Explore a finished dashboard, panel by panel, to see what it monitors and how each panel serves that purpose.
Find the **Memory / CPU** panel, top left.
This panel answers the question: How much memory and CPU is the server using, and how has that changed over time? The title names the two resources it measures, so you can read it without opening it.
Focus on the **Memory** gauge in the bottom row.
This panel answers the question: How close is memory use to its limit? It's the same resource as the first panel, shown as one value within a range instead of a line over time.
Focus on **server requests**, below Memory / CPU.
These two answer the question: How many people are signing in, and how many requests is the server handling, over time? They measure what the service is doing rather than the machine it runs on.

Four panels carry this title: two bar gauges on the right, and a gauge and a third bar gauge in the bottom row. One title, four displays. Nothing on the panels says how they differ, so the viewer can't tell which one to read.

The titles are what the viewer has to go on. Read together, they describe one server: the resources it uses and the traffic it handles. That is what this dashboard monitors, and it's the question to hold in mind as you read each panel.
You've seen what this dashboard monitors, how each panel's title tells you what it measures, and which panels repeat. Next, see how a panel gets the data behind its title.
